source.title: To Use or not to Use Muon: How Simplicity Bias in Optimizers Matters
source.authors: Sara Dragutinovi'c; Yedi Zhang; R. Ranganath

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Reports generalization results for optimizer choices in toy feature-learning, routing, and transformer tasks. It does not test random-label fitting or the specific behaviors in V1–V6.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on spurious-feature and shared-structure generalization, but no experiment randomly labels training images or tests fitting random labels, shuffled pixels, Gaussian-noise inputs, or the claim's other specified conditions. These generalization results are recorded under fits_no_version. Cited memorization findings from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Arpit et al. as background on simplicity bias, but its own results measure predictive-feature reliance, shared representations and extrapolation. It does not compare learning real versus random labels, measure random-label interpolation, or test any other V1–V6 condition. Gaussian regression inputs with structured targets and numerical noise in optimizer updates do not establish V3 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors argue that Muon and its Spectral GD simplification gain speed while losing forms of dynamical simplicity bias, which can impair shared-structure discovery and generalization in their small toy tasks. They explicitly make spurious-feature performance dependent on data properties and leave larger-scale implications unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies optimizer dynamics and generalization on toy feature-learning, routing, and cycle tasks, not random-label fitting or the original sources’ random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The relative performance on the digit and spurious pixel features changes with pixel intensity; the paper says the optimizer that performs better depends on the data properties. Transformer results also vary across task and architecture ablations, including loss, layer normalization, MLPs, head count, rank, and curriculum.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD relies on the digit feature longer, while Muon uses the predictive pixel earlier; their final feature preferences differ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice changes predictive-feature reliance, and its generalization benefit depends on feature strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Both routing optimizers converge on trained pairings, but SGD generalizes to unseen source pairings whereas Spectral GD generalizes poorly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer bias can determine whether a structured routing task yields shared representations.

fits_no_version.finding: In the base cycle task, SGD extrapolates to the withheld skip better than Muon; tested Muon weight-decay increases do not help.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects withheld-skip extrapolation in the tested transformer setup.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to small-scale toy tasks and qualitative outcomes; several values are available only in figures, and the authors state that larger-scale Muon behavior remains unanswered. The linear-attention analysis relies on stated assumptions, including joint diagonalizability for the formal result.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results omitted. Other optimizer/task ablations are discussed qualitatively or shown in figures, but do not test any of V1–V6.

untested.parts: All parts: random-label training accuracy, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
All parts: relative training time on true and random labels and convergence versus corruption fraction.
Zero-error fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test performance across label-corruption fractions.
Regularization failing to prevent random-label fitting and generalization on true labels after removing regularization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels and differences between real- and random-label learning trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T3 classification to cites_only/T6. None of the rows warrants a verdict on V1–V6. Here cannot_determine means the measure cannot establish a claim-version effect; it does not dispute the reported optimizer result.

versions.untested_parts: Random labeling, training error, test error at chance, and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time for true versus random labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across fractions of corrupted labels.
Whether regularization prevents random-label fitting or whether removing it harms generalization on true labels.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels, and how those labels differ over training.

rows.subject: CNN
rows.size_stated: 2 convolutional layers followed by 2 linear layers; 32 and 64 filters; first fully connected layer output dimension 128; second dimension 10
rows.operation_detail: Compared SGD and Muon accuracy on the digit-only and test evaluators during digit and pixel feature learning.

conditions.value: MNIST digit feature plus predictive pixel feature

rows.measure: Accuracy over training; generalization to digit-only evaluator
rows.value: The SGD curves separate only at the peak accuracy on Digit set; the model pursues a solution relying only on the digit feature for much longer.
rows.note: Qualitative result; no accuracy values are stated in the text.
rows.check: The qualitative feature-reliance result is supported, but neither feature involves random or noisy training labels; its state cannot describe any claim version.

rows.measure: Correctness of learned function on unseen input-output source pairs
rows.value: Solves the task for input-output pairs seen during training, but generalization is poor on pairs absent from training; both algorithms achieve perfect convergence.
rows.note: The paper describes memorizing seen pairs and poor generalization qualitatively; no numeric metric is given.
rows.check: Perfect convergence and poor generalization concern structured routing targets. The authors' characterization as memorization does not establish random-label memorization.
